stages.name: Native peoples
stages.desc: Iberians, Celts, Ligurians and Numidians, trading with all comers

stages.name: Etruscan
stages.desc: Etruscan cities lead the trade of the coast

stages.name: Massaliot Greek
stages.desc: Massalia and its trading posts dominate the coast

stages.name: Carthaginian
stages.desc: Carthage controls the land or its trade

stages.name: Roman
stages.desc: Rome rules or leads the land

states.name: France
timeline: Etruscan wine and black bucchero pottery dominate the trade of southern Gaul; Phocaean Greeks found Massalia
Massaliot wine amphorae replace Etruscan imports along the Gulf of Lion and up the Rhône
Massalia founds Agathe (Agde) at the mouth of the Hérault
Olbia (Hyères) is founded as a fortified post; Pytheas sails from Massalia for the far north
Antipolis (Antibes) and Nikaia (Nice) extend Massaliot posts east toward Italy
A Roman army lands at Massalia as Hannibal crosses the Rhône

states.name: Spain
timeline: Iberians and the kingdom of Tartessos; Phoenician colonies at Gadir and Malaka on the south coast
Phocaean Greeks found Emporion on the Catalan coast, a trading post later tied to Massalia
Tartessos fades; Carthage takes over the Phoenician south, Massaliot posts trade on the east coast
Hamilcar Barca lands at Gadir and begins a Carthaginian conquest of southern Spain
Hasdrubal founds New Carthage; the Ebro treaty with Rome follows about 226 BC
Hannibal takes Saguntum after an eight-month siege
Gnaeus Scipio lands at Emporion and wins the coast north of the Ebro
Roman and Massaliot ships destroy the Carthaginian fleet at the mouth of the Ebro

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage, a Phoenician colony, is becoming the leading power of the west
Defeated at Himera in Sicily, Carthage expands across north Africa
Agathocles of Syracuse lands in Africa and threatens Carthage
Defeat in the First Punic War; the unpaid mercenaries revolt

states.name: Italy
timeline: Etruscan cities lead Tyrrhenian trade; Greek colonies hold the south and Sicily
Rome expels its last Etruscan king and signs a first treaty with Carthage
Syracuse breaks Etruscan sea power off Cumae
Rome destroys the Etruscan city of Veii
Victory at Sentinum makes Rome master of central Italy
Rome wins Sicily at the end of the First Punic War
Rome seizes Sardinia and Corsica from Carthage

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Numidian and Libyan peoples; Phoenician anchorages along the coast
Carthaginian trading towns line the coast from Hippo to Iol
Numidian kings rule the interior as allies of Carthage

events.title: Massalia founded
events.text: Phocaean Greeks settle beside the Lacydon inlet; legend says their leader Protis married Gyptis, daughter of a local king.

events.title: First sea victory
events.text: Thucydides records that the Phocaeans founding Massalia defeated the Carthaginians at sea.

events.title: Carthage rising
events.text: Carthage, founded by Tyre, is taking charge of the Phoenician west.

events.title: Emporion
events.text: Phocaean traders settle on an islet at Empúries, the start of Greek trade in Catalonia.

events.title: Alalia founded
events.text: Phocaeans found Alalia on the east coast of Corsica.

events.title: Refugees from Phocaea
events.text: Persia takes Phocaea in Ionia; its refugees sail west to Alalia and Massalia.

events.title: Battle of Alalia
events.text: Sixty Phocaean ships fight 120 Etruscan and Carthaginian ships; they win but lose forty and abandon Corsica.

events.title: Elea founded
events.text: Survivors of Alalia found Elea on the coast south of Naples.

events.title: Euthymenes sails
events.text: The Massaliot Euthymenes sails out past the Pillars of Heracles and down the coast of Africa.

events.title: Wine for the Celts
events.text: Massaliot amphorae and Greek bronzes travel up the Rhône; a great Greek krater is later buried at Vix.

events.title: First Roman treaty
events.text: Rome and Carthage agree spheres of trade; Romans may not sail beyond the Fair Promontory.

events.title: Hemeroskopeion
events.text: A Massaliot post with a temple of Artemis stands on the headland of Dénia.

events.title: Heracleides' tactic
events.text: Sosylus credits Massaliots with a second line of ships learned from Heracleides at an 'Artemisium', perhaps here.

events.title: Himera
events.text: Greek Syracuse and Akragas crush a Carthaginian army in Sicily.

events.title: Battle of Cumae
events.text: Hiero of Syracuse destroys an Etruscan fleet off Cumae.

events.title: Fishing wars
events.text: Justin says Massalia often beat Carthage in wars sparked by seized fishing boats.

events.title: Lattara
events.text: Massaliot merchants trade wine for grain at the Celtic port of Lattara.

events.title: Agathe
events.text: Massalia founds Agathe (Agde) at the mouth of the Hérault.

events.title: Rome's ransom
events.text: After the Gauls sack Rome, Massalia helps pay the ransom, Justin says.

events.title: Rhode
events.text: Rhode (Roses), on the bay north of Emporion, strikes its own coins.

events.title: Second treaty
events.text: A new treaty bars Romans from trading beyond Mastia in southern Spain.

events.title: Pytheas sails
events.text: Pytheas of Massalia sails past Gades to Britain and the northern seas.

events.title: Olbia
events.text: Massalia builds a square fortified post at Olbia, near Hyères.

events.title: Agathocles
events.text: Agathocles of Syracuse lands in Africa and besieges Carthage's lands.

events.title: First Punic War
events.text: Rome and Carthage go to war over Messana in Sicily.

events.title: Mylae
events.text: Rome's new fleet wins its first sea battle against Carthage.

events.title: Aegates Islands
events.text: A Roman victory at sea ends the First Punic War; Carthage gives up Sicily.

events.title: Sardinia seized
events.text: Rome takes Sardinia and Corsica while Carthage fights its mercenaries.

events.title: Hamilcar in Spain
events.text: Hamilcar Barca lands at Gades to build a new Carthaginian empire in Spain.

events.title: Roman envoys
events.text: A Roman embassy questions Hamilcar about his aims in Spain, Cassius Dio reports.

events.title: Hamilcar drowns
events.text: Hamilcar dies fighting the Oretani near Helike; his son-in-law Hasdrubal takes command.

events.title: New Carthage
events.text: Hasdrubal founds New Carthage, a great harbour facing the Balearics.

events.title: Ebro treaty
events.text: Hasdrubal agrees not to cross the Ebro in arms, shielding Massalia's Spanish allies.

events.title: Hannibal commands
events.text: Hasdrubal is murdered; the army chooses Hamilcar's son Hannibal.

events.title: Saguntum falls
events.text: Hannibal takes Rome's friend Saguntum after an eight-month siege.

events.title: Rhône crossing
events.text: Massaliot guides lead Scipio's cavalry to find Hannibal crossing the Rhône.

events.title: Scipio at Emporion
events.text: Gnaeus Scipio lands at Emporion and wins the coast north of the Ebro.

events.title: Cissa
events.text: Gnaeus Scipio defeats Hanno near Tarraco and captures his baggage.

events.title: Battle of the Ebro
events.text: Two Massaliot scouts find the Carthaginian fleet; Scipio's attack captures twenty-five ships.

chartNote: Share of the area of five present-day countries (France, Spain, Italy, Tunisia, Algeria), by the power that dominated each one's coastal trade or ruled it. Regions are today's boundaries. This is a simplification: coasts were shared, interiors mostly stayed native, and Massalia's trading posts appear as events. Algeria's size swings the shares; ancient dates are approximate.
